findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:93 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseResult wrapper ({success, data}) instead of the parsed payload, but it is stored directly as the credential (data: { key }); previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the data itself, so stored credentials become {success:true, data:{...}} and Google auth breaks on next use in both sync and non-sync modes

[High/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:12-19 — in sync mode it returns the raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google reads res?.data (undefined on a fetch Response), Hubspot casts it to the SDK HubspotToken (fields undefined → NaN expiry), zoho-bigin/zohocrm read axios-style .data (TypeError on undefined); the sync path is broken/crashes for these apps and the response body is never parsed or status-checked

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8-11 — [z.string().toString()] evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]" (both computed keys collide, second overwrites first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema effectively only requires access_token; expiry fields are stripped, not captured, contradicting the comment and losing expiry data in sync mode

[Medium/data] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 — injects placeholder refresh_token: "refresh_token" into the parsed data whenever the response lacks one; office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~264 spreads this into o365AuthCredentials and persists it, overwriting the real refresh token with the placeholder and permanently breaking future refreshes

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:14 — the schema-mode switch doesn't account for userId, unlike refreshOAuthTokens: for team credentials (userId null) the local provider refresh runs, but the response is still parsed with the minimal schema, stripping expiry/refresh_token from a legitimate local refresh and corrupting the stored key
[Medium/security] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:22-25 — webhook secret compared with !== (not constant-time); use crypto.timingSafeEqual to avoid timing attacks on the shared secret

[Medium/security] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10-19 — the POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret/API key/header), so the endpoint cannot verify the caller; anyone who can reach it can request credentials for an arbitrary calcomUserId/appSlug

[Medium/bug] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:29,55 — schema.parse(req.body), symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse all throw on malformed input, producing unhandled 500s; should safeParse and return 4xx with a meaningful message

[Medium/concurrency] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-85 — findFirst-then-create with no unique constraint or transaction; concurrent webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appId) create duplicate credentials

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~90 — with sync mode enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the minimal schema, which strips instance_url (and other fields) from the Salesforce token response; the persisted key loses instance_url and the jsforce connection breaks

[Medium/performance] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-97 — the token refresh runs unconditionally on every service instantiation (no expiry check), adding an OAuth round-trip plus a credential DB write to every calendar operation even when the access token is still valid

[Medium/test_gap] no tests were added for the new webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, or parseRefreshTokenResponse, despite these being security- and data-sensitive paths exhibiting the wrapper/placeholder behaviors above
[Low/bug] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~85 — response.statusText !== "OK" is fragile (statusText is empty under HTTP/2 and in some runtimes); use response.ok instead

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:22-24 — the configured header name is not lowercased before lookup; Node lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME silently fails auth (fail-closed, but hard to debug)

[Low/data] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:55-58 — decrypted keys are persisted without validating them against the app's credential schema; a structurally wrong (but valid JSON) payload is stored and only surfaces as runtime failures inside the app services later

[Low/doc_defect] .env.example:241-243 — comment states the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256" but suggests openssl rand -base64 24, which produces 24 bytes of entropy (32 base64 characters); the inconsistent guidance leads to invalid-key-length errors for self-hosters following it literally

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:14 — the schema-mode switch doesn't account for userId, unlike refreshOAuthTokens: for team credentials (userId null) the local provider refresh runs, but the response is still parsed with the minimal schema, stripping expiry/refresh_token from a legitimate local refresh and corrupting the stored key

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `refreshOAuthTokens` only switches to the remote sync endpoint when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (so team creds with `userId` null use the local provider refresh). But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to the minimal schema based only on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, with no `userId` check. This mismatch is verifiable in the new files. For team credentials (or any local refresh when the endpoint env var is set), the token response will still be parsed with the minimal schema, which (as a `z.object`) will strip unknown keys like `refresh_token`, then the helper forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the string "refresh_token". Call sites like Office365 merge `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials, so this can overwrite a real refresh token and corrupt persisted keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:22-25 — webhook secret compared with !== (not constant-time); use crypto.timingSafeEqual to avoid timing attacks on the shared secret

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook endpoint authenticates requests by directly comparing the provided header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts). This is not a constant-time comparison and can theoretically leak information about the shared secret via timing differences, which is a security defect in an auth check introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10-19 — the POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret/API key/header), so the endpoint cannot verify the caller; anyone who can reach it can request credentials for an arbitrary calcomUserId/appSlug

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the branch that calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and does not include any auth header/secret. The diff also introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, but those are only used to authenticate the inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), not this outbound sync call. This is a concrete, diff-grounded security design concern for the new credential-sync integration, though whether it becomes an actual vulnerability depends on how the external endpoint is implemented and exposed (the code even comments “Customize the payload…”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-85 — findFirst-then-create with no unique constraint or transaction; concurrent webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appId) create duplicate credentials

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the code does a non-atomic `findFirst` on `{ userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }` and then conditionally `create` (else branch) without a transaction or `upsert` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, ~lines 60-85). This is a real concurrency risk: simultaneous webhook deliveries for the same pair could both observe “no row” and attempt `create`, which can either produce duplicates (if no DB uniqueness) or throw on a unique constraint (if one exists). The diff doesn’t show the Prisma schema, so the claim about “no unique constraint” / guaranteed duplicates can’t be fully verified, but the race condition concern is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~90 — with sync mode enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the minimal schema, which strips instance_url (and other fields) from the Salesforce token response; the persisted key loses instance_url and the jsforce connection breaks

adjudication.rationale: In SalesforceCalendarService, the refresh flow now parses the Salesforce token response via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then persists `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ... }`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` ignores the provided `schema` whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is truthy, using `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead. That minimal schema does not declare `instance_url` (and Zod `z.object(...)` will strip unknown keys by default), so in “sync mode” the persisted credential key can lose `instance_url`, breaking later jsforce usage that depends on it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-97 — the token refresh runs unconditionally on every service instantiation (no expiry check), adding an OAuth round-trip plus a credential DB write to every calendar operation even when the access token is still valid

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the added logic fetches a new access token and updates the credential in Prisma unconditionally during service initialization (lines shown in diff around the new `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token")` and subsequent `prisma.credential.update(...)`), with no check of existing token validity/expiry. This means every time `SalesforceCalendarService` is instantiated it performs an OAuth round-trip and DB write even if the access token is still valid, matching the performance concern in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] no tests were added for the new webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, or parseRefreshTokenResponse, despite these being security- and data-sensitive paths exhibiting the wrapper/placeholder behaviors above

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new security/data-sensitive logic—a new webhook endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) that authenticates via a secret header and decrypts/stores credentials, plus new OAuth-refresh wrappers (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) that change token-refresh behavior and include placeholder behavior (e.g., setting `refresh_token` to a dummy string when missing). No test files or test changes are included in the diff to cover these new code paths or their edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:22-24 — the configured header name is not lowercased before lookup; Node lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME silently fails auth (fail-closed, but hard to debug)

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the secret check indexes `req.headers[...]` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` directly. Node/Next normalize incoming header names to lowercase in `req.headers`, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is configured with any uppercase letters, the lookup will miss and the request will be rejected with "Invalid webhook secret". The diff adds only a comment in .env.example saying it "Should be in lowercase" but does not enforce `.toLowerCase()` in code, so the behavior is fragile and can silently fail auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:55-58 — decrypted keys are persisted without validating them against the app's credential schema; a structurally wrong (but valid JSON) payload is stored and only surfaces as runtime failures inside the app services later

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the decrypted `keys` payload is obtained via `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` with no validation against any app-specific credential schema (only `userId/appSlug/keys` string are validated by zod). This means structurally invalid-but-JSON data can be persisted and would only fail later when services assume a specific credential shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] .env.example:241-243 — comment states the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256" but suggests openssl rand -base64 24, which produces 24 bytes of entropy (32 base64 characters); the inconsistent guidance leads to invalid-key-length errors for self-hosters following it literally

adjudication.rationale: In `.env.example` the new comments for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` state the key “must be 32 bytes for AES256” but suggest generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which yields 24 bytes of random data (encoded to ~32 base64 chars). The inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and could mislead self-hosters, but it’s a documentation/config guidance issue rather than a verifiable runtime defect from the code shown (no key-length validation is present in this diff).
